text:
samantha: Heads-up — hit a weird cancel/fencepost bug in the Go SDK generator while onboarding a sample app. Repro is tiny, putting it here.

samantha: Steps: start generator stream, read first few chunks, cancel ctx, but goroutine stays around and kv cache isn't released. Not seeing cancel callback.

samantha: Repro snippet: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, err := client.Generator(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
// read one item
item, ok := iter.Next()
// then cancel
cancel()
// expecting iter.Close/Next to return quickly but it blocks
```

jorge: hmm can you paste the exact client call shape? is this the new Generator.Iter API or the older stream helper?

samantha: Generator.Iter (the Pull-style iterator we shipped in the demo). Using default auth refresher provider.

olivia: did you try calling iter.Close() after cancel? we have a Close method but I know its semantics aren't always consistent.

samantha: yep, Close() also blocks sometimes. The stack shows a goroutine stuck in runtime.(*mcache).nextFree or something around the recv on a channel inside gen.go handshake.

jorge: could be a race between auth refresh and the handshake goroutine. We had a similar pattern where refresh spawns a background token retrier that keeps the stream alive until a message arrives.

olivia: @samantha any chance the sampleapp is using a parent context with deadline? I've seen deadline propagation + iteration cause weird late-cancel semantics.

samantha: The parent is background. I reproduced in a minimal test: https://git.redwood/repro/gen-fencepost (private link). Test case is literally: start, call Next once, cancel, wait 100ms, assert no goroutines.

jorge: thanks. Can you attach the goroutine dump? Also what's the Go version? we saw subtle scheduler differences on 1.20 vs 1.21.

samantha: Go 1.21. Dump attached in repro. Key goroutine shows waiting on a channel recv inside the generator handshake loop: `for { select { case msg := <-protoCh: ... case <-ctx.Done(): ... } }` but ctx.Done() didn't fire for that goroutine.

olivia: that sounds like the ctx used by that goroutine might be a child created by the auth layer that never receives cancel if the parent cancel path uses a separate cancel function. Could be we forgot to thread the parent ctx into the auth refresher.

jorge: if true, fix is probably to pass the original ctx into the token refresher and ensure any spawned goroutines select on that ctx.Done. But we should also improve ergonomics: generator API should expose a WithContext or return an io.Closer pattern to make it explicit.

olivia: agree. Proposal: change Generator.Iter to return (iter, cancelFunc) or have iter implement io.ReadCloser semantics and make Close non-blocking after a grace period, returning an error if still draining.

samantha: I like `io.ReadCloser` analogy — familiar to Go devs. Could also add a docs blurb about cancel propagation and recommended patterns.

jorge: quick workaround — call cancel and then concurrently call iter.Close with a timeout: 
```go
go func() { time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond); iter.ForceClose() }()
// ForceClose is a hack we could add quickly in dev SDK builds
```

olivia: let's file a GH issue and a follow-up PR. @jorge can you owner the fix for token refresher? i'll do the API ergonomics proposal (small RFC in devex repo).

jorge: yep i'll triage the goroutine dump now.

devex-bot: Issue created: DEX-4823 "generator iterator cancel fencepost — auth refresher leak" (assigned to jorge) :white_check_mark:

samantha: thanks y'all — repro link + tiny test in issue. will add a short note to the onboarding guide until we ship fix. :+1:
